parsed.explanation: The combined regime is hostile: national law criminalises same-sex conduct/gross indecency and reaches foreigners; subnational Sharia adds gender-expression penalties for Muslims and court-ordered religious rehabilitation. Documented police and religious raids, mass arrests including foreign nationals, delayed release, male-ward sexual violence, official “full licence” enforcement against transgender persons, and killings show severe consequences if a visitor is outed. Dated record says tourists are rarely targeted, and courts, legal aid, and embassies sometimes obtain release, but no operative traveler protection, anti-discrimination, or facility guidance exists. For adults travelling with minors, age-specific rules are not documented; the same discretionary criminal/rehabilitation regime would apply, and a child’s exposure is uncertain but not reduced. Score low in high-risk band.

entry_documents.exposure: No explicit trans entry ban. Passport marker/name mismatch friction not documented; 2001 statement about deporting gay minister operational status unclear. Visitor could still be screened under broad morality norms.
entry_documents.interaction: Foreign documents are carried; if discovery at check-in/security, discretionary referral is possible into investigation.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Mass raids have arrested hundreds, including 31 foreign nationals; delayed release after magistrate rejected remand. Arbitrary arrest, detention, male-ward placement, sexual violence, and official strip-search/assault are documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Legal aid mobilised bail; embassies intervened; courts sometimes rejected remand or narrowed state provisions.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: An identity/presentation encounter can escalate to Penal Code or religious enforcement custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Penal Code applies nationally to any person; Sharia provisions apply to Muslims, including cross-dressing and religious counselling/rehabilitation for up to one year in some states.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Some state religious provisions struck down on federalism; Penal Code remains.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal criminal exposure and state religious exposure combine; Muslim visitors face harsher subnational rules.

care_services.exposure: Discriminatory denial of health care is documented for trans people, but visitor-specific emergency/HRT denial is not documented. Blood donation ban signals climate.
care_services.interaction: Illness or injury could force disclosure; care refusal may interact with police custody.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Officials gave religious departments full licence to enforce against transgender persons; trans woman hunted by officers; venue/media raids and entertainment law bans LGBTQ promotion are documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: International condemnation and court actions narrowed some provisions, but did not remove Penal Code risk.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing guides police/religious raids and discretionary targeting of visible trans travelers.

minors_guardians.exposure: No youth-specific rules documented. General gender-expression criminalisation, rehabilitation, and arbitrary arrest could affect a minor; a parent/guardian encounter may reveal the child’s status.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family travel does not create exemption; minor remains under combined criminal/religious enforcement regime.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: A pattern of trans women killed (third in under two months, 2019), police mistreatment and impunity is documented, though recency and rate are weak.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Communications hate-speech code covers sexual orientation; some courts/NGOs intervene after incidents.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Public violence plus state targeting lowers likelihood police protect a trans visitor.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination or hate-crime protection; gender-marker changes are rejected; border, detention, facility, and minor-care procedures are unclear.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Bailors, legal aid, consular intervention, and occasional remand refusals reduce immediate detention risk.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies can shorten detention but do not prevent arrest or severe penalties if charged.

anchor_checks.comparison: Compared with routine visitor document-arrest and months in custody here, tourists are not routinely targeted and consular/legal aid helped release. Still, severe Penal Code whipping, male-ward violence, and official targeting keep this near or below 0.15 rather than safer.

Similar to morality provisions selectively used against queer people, but this dossier has national 20-year/whipping exposure, documented foreign arrests, religious rehabilitation, and state-sanctioned targeting, so it is materially worse than 0.25-D.

Unlike universal address/database registration, exposure is episodic; however, consequences after discovery are far more severe—long imprisonment, whipping, sexual violence, and official trans enforcement—so this rates below 0.45-D.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime layers federal criminalization with state religious enforcement. A visitor who is outed may face discretionary public-morality scrutiny, raid or report, arrest, delayed release, male-ward custody, sexual violence, or religious rehabilitation; for Muslims, cross-dressing/counselling rules add direct gender-expression punishment. Tourists rarely targeted and some judicial/consular/NGO interventions reduce duration, but they are not protections because they address only after exposure and leave severe penal outcomes intact. The absence of anti-discrimination, facility guidance, care rules, and minor-specific safeguards compounds uncertainty. Old trans killings are not treated as current prevalence, but the documented official targeting and violent custody make severity decisive.
